biur-halacha/9:_.en: If he did not stipulate on it initially — apparently his intent is like regarding sukkah decoration explained in siman 638 that one must stipulate beforehand on erev Shemini Atzeret that he is not separating himself from enjoying it. However per Bikkurei Yaakov siman 653 it suffices if he stipulates before performing the mitzvah that it not become forbidden through the mitzvah, since he does not separate himself from enjoyment; the same for hadas forbidden to smell all seven because it was set aside for its mitzvah — stipulating before the mitzvah that he not separate from enjoyment suffices. But in the essential law whether a condition helps, Magen Avraham proved this depends on the dispute of Rashba and Ran (and Sefer Yereim and Hagahot Maimoni — the full Yereim manuscript states explicitly that a condition helps). According to them a condition helps even for that day; according to Tosafot it does not help here. It implies for aravah and etrog that even if he separated after the first day a condition does not permit enjoyment that day — I do not understand well his proof, for here we discuss aravah used only on the seventh day; why should Tosafot not allow a condition that day? We have no proof from Tosafot except for the first day when it lacks validity and one cannot stipulate on erev Shemini Atzeret not to separate from enjoyment like etz sukkah; but on other days when separated while still valid, such as etrog and aravah when its top was cut (invalid only for hadar, and most poskim hold hadar is not meakev except first day), certainly even for Tosafot a condition helps when he stipulates he will not separate from taking a little, for Tosafot mean it is set aside only from complete consumption but one may take a little and leave enough for validity without a condition; nevertheless there is a difference: per Tosafot one may take only more than the minimum before the mitzvah but not consume entirely even after the mitzvah, for it was set aside for that and holiness applies until the festival ends if he did not stipulate; but if he stipulated he does not separate, no holiness applies, and immediately after the mitzvah he may take aravah branches to roast meat and fruit and consume entirely — as in Beitzah 40b. Therefore they take the aravah separately, hinting that on the seventh day there is separation and the wicked are judged separately and lowered to the earth; therefore they beat them on the ground to humble them. Or to show that the success of the wicked is only so they may later be humbled, as Midrash on the verse regarding the enemies of Hashem. Therefore we show that although the aravah merited to be raised with the lulav and its kind to join together, it is only to humble them afterward to the earth — this ascent is their descent. In sum, it is proper at the time of beating the aravah to intend to humble the wicked and fulfill the verse that the wicked shall be as ashes under their soles — this is the plain intention of this aravah.
